newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sees inflation targets in reach.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sees inflation targets in reach.

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank said on Tuesday that prospects of meeting inflation targets in the next two years were good and the chances of achieving three to four percent economic growth in 1996/97 were probable.
In an inflation report, the bank said it also saw further room for lowering its key interest rate, the repo, which is its key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
But the Riksbank said cost pressure from wages was a source of concern in respect to future inflation.
The economic slowdown towards the end of 1995 had been brief, the central bank said, and there had been recovery during the current year.
Although its main economic forecasts remained unchanged, the Riksbank said economic growth could be slightly better than previously envisaged.
"A total growth rate of three to four percent for 1996 and 1997 combined is still considered most probable, though today the emphasis is in the upper half of this interval," the Riksbank said.
